name: Eleazar
description: One of the principal scribes, an aged man of fourscore and ten years and of a well-favoured countenance; constrained to eat swine's flesh, he spit it out and went willingly to the torment and died, choosing not to stain his old age with hypocrisy, and leaving a notable example of courage to the young

points: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine's flesh. So the Greeks wanted Eleazar to eat swine's flesh.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine's flesh. So Eleazar was an aged man, of a well favoured countenance, with a great report amongst the Israelites.

Now this was the time of that wicked king Antiochus. He was trying to make one of our aged men, Eleazar, open his mouth and eat pig's flesh. I do not know what it is about Esau and eating pig's flesh. They love to have us eat pork. And when you tell them you do not eat it, they will be like, oh, are you Muslim? No. We do not eat pig, Esau. We do not.

For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion. That is ninety years old. So they wanted him to influence the young generation.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion. Ninety years old, and he would not pretend, because we have to be examples to the younger generation.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: For it becometh not our age, said he, in any wise to dissemble, whereby many young persons might think that Eleazar, being fourscore years old and ten, were now gone to a strange religion. Listen to what he said. He said, no, I am not doing it. Why am I not doing it? Because I do not want young people to think that I have gone to a strange religion. He did not want the people under him, the younger brothers and sisters in the congregation, to think that he had gone off. So he would rather die than live with that stain. But today our people say, I don't care, I don't care what you think about me. No. Our forefathers thought on their good report. They thought on their good report, and they would change in order to have a good report. No, I am not going to do that, because I do not want any stain on my name.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org

cases.name: Eleazar the scribe
cases.charge: Choosing to die gloriously rather than eat swine’s flesh, or pretend to, at ninety years old
